newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank Canada plans merchant bank unit.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank Canada plans merchant bank unit.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada said on Tuesday that it planned to establish a merchant banking subsidiary with an initial capital commitment of C$500 million.
Subject to regulatory approval, the Toronto-based subsidiary is expected to commence business on January 1, 1997, Royal Bank said in a statement.
"A merchant bank aligned with a strong investment banking and equity research capability is a powerful combination," said John Cleghorn, Royal Bank's chairman and chief executive officer.

The merchant bank subsidiary will be jointly managed by George Engman, former head of the Merchant Banking Group of the Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board, and Philip Olsson, former vice-chairman of RBC Dominion Securities.
Anthony Fell, chairman and chief executive officer of RBC Dominion Securities, will be chairman of the merchant bank.

The bank said the structure of its newest subsidiary will enable it to accept outside risk capital provided by strategic partners. The merchant bank will focus primarily on investment opportunities in Canada and abroad, the bank said.
